deck_name: 君の名は。 Ch.7 うつくしく、もがく — Vocabulary
source: 新海誠『君の名は。』(角川つばさ文庫), 第七章「うつくしく、もがく」
notes: Back in her own body after the twilight meeting, 三葉 races down the mountain while the plan unfolds: テッシー cuts the town's power, サヤちん broadcasts the evacuation call, and the town office contradicts it. As the comet splits overhead, 三葉 falls, finds an unexpected message on her palm, and pushes on to confront her father before the fragment falls. The deck focuses on physical struggle, darkness and confusion, the comet as spectacle, despair and resolve, and aftermath words. The list is built from the chapter's scenes and the novel's style, not transcribed page by page, so a few words may sit a chapter early or late — especially the aftermath cards (奇跡, 生存, 無事, 訓練, 大半), which may belong to the start of Ch.8. Words and patterns already taught in an earlier chapter's deck aren't repeated here, even when this chapter uses them again.

priority_guide.high: Learn before or while reading this chapter — it carries the scene.
priority_guide.medium: Useful; context usually helps if you forget it.
priority_guide.low: Recognition is enough — look it up once, don't over-drill.

difficulty_guide.two_above: N1 / literary — ambitious; learn to recognise it.

kanji_difficulty_guide.easy: Kanji are common; readable at N3.
kanji_difficulty_guide.medium: One or more kanji may trip you — drill the reading.
kanji_difficulty_guide.hard: Rare kanji or irregular reading — learn the kana form first.

meanings: to flounder (trying to get free or succeed)
cards.scene: The chapter title itself — 三葉 struggling with everything she has to save the town while the comet blazes overhead.
cards.context: Originally physical: thrashing your arms and legs to get free (水の中でもがく). Figuratively, to struggle desperately against a situation. Usually written in kana (the kanji 踠く is rare); the title pairs it with うつくしく, so the struggle itself is framed as something beautiful.
cards.example_sentence: どんなにもがいても、時間は止まってくれない。
cards.example_reading: どんなに もがいて も、 じかん は とまって くれない。
cards.example_meaning: No matter how much you struggle, time won't stop for you.

meanings: to run down (a slope or stairs)
cards.scene: Back in her own body after the twilight meeting, 三葉 races down the mountain toward the festival town.
cards.context: 駆ける (to run, dash — more literary than 走る) + 下りる. Its relatives: 駆け上がる (dash up), 駆け寄る (run up to someone), 駆け込む (rush into). 駆 has the horse radical 馬 — think galloping.
cards.example_sentence: 瀧は駅の階段を一気に駆け下りた。
cards.example_reading: たき は えき の かいだん を いっき に かけおりた。
cards.example_meaning: Taki dashed down the station stairs in one go.

cards.scene: 三葉 runs so hard and so long, down the mountain and through town, that she can barely breathe.
cards.context: Literally 'to cut one's breath'. Often 息を切らして + verb: 息を切らして走ってきた (came running, out of breath). Intransitive partner: 息が切れる (to run out of breath). Compare 息を呑む (gasp in surprise) and 息を殺す (hold your breath to stay hidden).
cards.example_sentence: 四葉は息を切らしながら、家まで走って帰ってきた。
cards.example_reading: よつは は いき を きらしながら、 いえ まで はしって かえって きた。
cards.example_meaning: Yotsuha ran all the way home, out of breath.

cards.scene: The sound of 三葉's breathing as she runs toward town without stopping.
cards.context: The sound of heavy breathing after exertion; also はあはあする / はあはあ言う. Rougher, wheezing breath is ぜえぜえ. Action-heavy prose often writes it in katakana: ハアハア.
cards.example_sentence: 五階まで階段で上ったら、はあはあと息が上がってしまった。
cards.example_reading: ごかい まで かいだん で のぼったら、 はあはあ と いき が あがって しまった。
cards.example_meaning: I took the stairs up to the fifth floor and ended up huffing and puffing.

cards.scene: Fits the narration of 三葉 pushing on toward town with every ounce of effort.
cards.context: The 懸命 inside 一生懸命, used alone in written style: 懸命に走る, 懸命な努力, 懸命の救助活動 (an all-out rescue effort — common in news). Don't confuse it with 賢明 (けんめい, wise), which sounds identical.
cards.example_sentence: 救助隊は夜通し懸命の捜索を続けた。
cards.example_reading: きゅうじょたい は よどおし けんめい の そうさく を つづけた。
cards.example_meaning: The rescue team kept up an all-out search through the night.

cards.scene: As exhaustion sets in on 三葉's run, her legs stop obeying her.
cards.context: もつれる (縺れる) = to get tangled, like thread. 足がもつれる = legs tangling from fatigue, alcohol or panic; 舌がもつれる = to slur one's words; 話がもつれる = a matter gets complicated.
cards.example_sentence: 疲れきって足がもつれ、彼は道の真ん中で転んだ。
cards.example_reading: つかれきって あし が もつれ、 かれ は みち の まんなか で ころんだ。
cards.example_meaning: Completely exhausted, his legs got tangled and he fell in the middle of the road.

cards.scene: After テッシー blows up the substation, the whole town is plunged into darkness.
cards.context: 暗 (dark) + 闇 (darkness). A dark place or pitch darkness: 暗闇の中で. 闇 (やみ) alone is more literary and metaphorical (闇夜, 心の闇). The blackout itself is 停電.
cards.example_sentence: 停電で、部屋は一瞬にして暗闇に包まれた。
cards.example_reading: ていでん で、 へや は いっしゅん に して くらやみ に つつまれた。
cards.example_meaning: In the power cut, the room was swallowed by darkness in an instant.

cards.scene: Fits the sudden hush of a festival town cut off from its lights, before the noise of confusion rises.
cards.context: 静まる (become quiet) + 返る, which here intensifies ('completely'), as in 呆れ返る. Usually past or ている form: しんと静まり返った夜 (a dead-silent night).
cards.example_sentence: 先生が入ってくると、騒がしかった教室が静まり返った。
cards.example_reading: せんせい が はいって くる と、 さわがしかった きょうしつ が しずまりかえった。
cards.example_meaning: When the teacher came in, the noisy classroom went completely silent.

cards.scene: The people of Itomori — the ones 三葉 and her friends are trying to move, and the ones every announcement addresses.
cards.context: 町 (town) + 民 (people). Official, broadcast-style word: announcements address 町民の皆さん. Parallel words: 市民 (city residents), 村民 (villagers), 住民 (residents in general), 国民 (a nation's citizens).
cards.example_sentence: 町民の皆さんは、落ち着いて行動してください。
cards.example_reading: ちょうみん の みなさん は、 おちついて こうどう して ください。
cards.example_meaning: Residents, please stay calm as you act.

cards.scene: Fits the uneasy festival crowd murmuring in the dark.
cards.context: From ざわざわ (murmuring, rustling). The noun ざわめき = a stir, a buzz of voices. Also leaves in the wind (木々がざわめく) or an uneasy heart (胸がざわめく).
cards.example_sentence: 有名人が現れると、会場がざわめいた。
cards.example_reading: ゆうめいじん が あらわれる と、 かいじょう が ざわめいた。
cards.example_meaning: When the celebrity appeared, a murmur ran through the hall.

cards.scene: Fits the festival crowd milling in the dark, unsure whether to move.
cards.context: 群 (flock, group) + 衆 (multitude). A large, unorganised crowd: 群衆をかき分ける (push through a crowd). 人混み is the everyday word for a crowded place; 群れ (むれ) = a flock or herd.
cards.example_sentence: 彼女は群衆をかき分けて、前へ進んだ。
cards.example_reading: かのじょ は ぐんしゅう を かきわけて、 まえ へ すすんだ。
cards.example_meaning: She pushed her way through the crowd and moved forward.

cards.scene: サヤちん's broadcast calls on the townspeople to evacuate.
cards.context: Noun from 呼びかける (to call out to; to appeal to the public). 避難の呼びかけ = a call to evacuate; 呼びかけに応じる = to respond to an appeal. It stresses urging people to act, not just shouting.
cards.example_sentence: 町の呼びかけに応じて、多くの人が清掃に参加した。
cards.example_reading: まち の よびかけ に おうじて、 おおく の ひと が せいそう に さんか した。
cards.example_meaning: In response to the town's appeal, many people joined the clean-up.

cards.scene: Fits the warnings broadcast over the town, which speak of the danger still to come.
cards.context: In warnings, 〜の恐れがある = there is a risk of ~: 火事の恐れ, 津波の恐れがある. As a plain noun it also means fear or dread (死への恐れ). Formal — news and emergency announcements love it.
cards.example_sentence: 大雨のため、川が氾濫する恐れがあります。
cards.example_reading: おおあめ の ため、 かわ が はんらん する おそれ が あります。
cards.example_meaning: Due to the heavy rain, there is a risk the river will flood.

cards.scene: The townspeople wait for official instructions — and get contradictory ones.
cards.context: 指 (point) + 示 (show). 指示を出す (give instructions), 指示に従う (follow instructions), 指示を待つ. 命令 is a harsher 'command'; 指示 is neutral direction from whoever is in charge.
cards.example_sentence: 係員の指示に従って、ゆっくり外に出てください。
cards.example_reading: かかりいん の しじ に したがって、 ゆっくり そと に でて ください。
cards.example_meaning: Please follow the staff's instructions and exit slowly.

cards.scene: The town office counters サヤちん's evacuation message, effectively cancelling it out.
cards.context: 打ち (emphatic prefix) + 消す. To deny a rumour (噂を打ち消す), to push away a feeling (不安を打ち消す), or in grammar, 打ち消し = the negative form. It means wiping something out by contradicting it.
cards.example_sentence: 彼は不安を打ち消すように、わざと明るく笑った。
cards.example_reading: かれ は ふあん を うちけす よう に、 わざと あかるく わらった。
cards.example_meaning: He laughed brightly on purpose, as if to push away his anxiety.

cards.scene: The town office's announcement tells people to stay where they are instead of evacuating.
cards.context: その場で待機 = wait where you are; その場で決める = decide on the spot; その場しのぎ = a stopgap. Points to the place or moment where something is happening.
cards.example_sentence: 地震が起きたら、まずその場で頭を守ってください。
cards.example_reading: じしん が おきたら、 まず そのば で あたま を まもって ください。
cards.example_meaning: When an earthquake hits, first protect your head right where you are.

cards.scene: The counter-announcement tells townspeople to stand by, and the evacuation stalls.
cards.context: 待 (wait) + 機 (opportunity). Waiting in readiness for orders: 自宅待機 (stay at home on standby), 待機する, 待機中. A formal, official word — which is why it sounds authoritative coming over a loudspeaker.
cards.example_sentence: 大雪のため、社員は自宅で待機するよう指示された。
cards.example_reading: おおゆき の ため、 しゃいん は じたく で たいき する よう しじ された。
cards.example_meaning: Because of the heavy snow, employees were told to stand by at home.

meanings: to shout at the top of one's lungs
cards.scene: Fits the shouting in the dark, confused town as people try to make themselves heard.
cards.context: 張り上げる = stretch up, raise high. Straining your voice so others can hear, not necessarily in anger (angry shouting is 怒鳴る). 声を限りに叫ぶ is a more dramatic 'scream with all your voice'.
cards.example_sentence: ガイドは観光客に向かって声を張り上げた。
cards.example_reading: ガイド は かんこうきゃく に むかって こえ を はりあげた。
cards.example_meaning: The guide raised her voice to call out to the tourists.

cards.scene: Fits Itomori voices urging people to hurry — the clipped western-Japan form of 早く.
cards.context: Shortened 早く (はやく → はよう → はよ), common across western Japan, including 飛騨弁-style Itomori speech: はよ逃げて (get out, quick!), はよして (hurry up). 関西弁 uses the same form.
cards.example_sentence: はよせんと、バスに乗り遅れるよ。
cards.example_reading: はよ せん と、 バス に のりおくれる よ。
cards.example_meaning: If you don't hurry, you'll miss the bus.

cards.scene: Fits the comet breaking up into pieces overhead.
cards.context: Breaking into many small pieces (割れる can be a single crack). Transitive: 砕く. 砕け散る = shatter and scatter. Figurative: 砕けた話し方 = relaxed, casual speech; 当たって砕けろ = go for it, even if you fail.
cards.example_sentence: コップが床に落ちて、粉々に砕けた。
cards.example_reading: コップ が ゆか に おちて、 こなごな に くだけた。
cards.example_meaning: The glass fell to the floor and shattered into tiny pieces.

cards.scene: The splitting comet is a breathtaking, dreamlike sight — beautiful even as it threatens the town.
cards.context: 幻想 (fantasy, illusion) + 的. A compliment for scenery and light: 幻想的な景色. It echoes the title's うつくしく — the terrible thing is also gorgeous.
cards.example_sentence: 雪の中のお祭りの灯りは、とても幻想的だった。
cards.example_reading: ゆき の なか の おまつり の あかり は、 とても げんそうてき だった。
cards.example_meaning: The festival lights in the snow were truly magical.

cards.scene: Running desperately, 三葉 trips and goes tumbling down a slope.
cards.context: Kanji 躓く is rare — learn the kana. 石につまずく (trip on a stone). Figuratively, to stumble at a task: 最初の問題でつまずく. 転ぶ means actually falling down; つまずく is catching your foot.
cards.example_sentence: 暗い道で石につまずいて、危うく転ぶところだった。
cards.example_reading: くらい みち で いし に つまずいて、 あやうく ころぶ ところ だった。
cards.example_meaning: I tripped on a stone on the dark road and nearly fell.

cards.scene: 三葉 falls and rolls helplessly down the slope.
cards.context: 転がる (roll) + 落ちる (fall). Compound verbs stack motion + direction: 転げ落ちる (a little more colloquial), 滑り落ちる (slide down). Figurative: 坂を転がり落ちるように = going downhill fast.
cards.example_sentence: ボールが階段を転がり落ちていった。
cards.example_reading: ボール が かいだん を ころがりおちて いった。
cards.example_meaning: The ball went rolling down the stairs.

cards.scene: Fits the moment 三葉 tumbles over and over down the slope.
cards.context: Many senses: heavy rolling (ごろごろ転がる), thunder (雷がごろごろ鳴る), lounging (家でごろごろする), and lots of something lying around (石がごろごろある). Lighter, smaller rolling is ころころ.
cards.example_sentence: 大きな岩がごろごろと坂を転がってきた。
cards.example_reading: おおきな いわ が ごろごろ と さか を ころがって きた。
cards.example_meaning: A large rock came rolling and tumbling down the slope.

cards.scene: After her fall down the slope, 三葉 is covered in mud and dirt.
cards.context: 泥 (mud) + だらけ (covered with, full of — usually something unwanted). Same pattern: 傷だらけ (covered in cuts), 間違いだらけ (full of mistakes). 泥まみれ is similar but stresses being smeared all over.
cards.example_sentence: サッカーの試合のあと、ユニフォームが泥だらけになった。
cards.example_reading: サッカー の しあい の あと、 ユニフォーム が どろだらけ に なった。
cards.example_meaning: After the soccer match, my uniform was covered in mud.

cards.scene: Fits the knees 三葉 bangs and scrapes in her tumble down the slope.
cards.context: A common word with a tricky kanji. 膝をつく (drop to one's knees), 膝を抱える (hug one's knees), 膝が笑う (legs go wobbly — literally 'knees laugh' — after a hard hike). Also 'lap': 膝の上に猫を乗せる.
cards.example_sentence: 山を下りるころには、膝が笑ってうまく歩けなかった。
cards.example_reading: やま を おりる ころ に は、 ひざ が わらって うまく あるけなかった。
cards.example_meaning: By the time we got down the mountain, my knees were wobbling and I could hardly walk.

cards.scene: Fits the scrapes 三葉 gets when she falls and rolls down the slope.
cards.context: 擦る (rub) + むく (剥く, peel). 膝を擦りむく, 手を擦りむく. Also written 擦り剥く. 擦り傷 (すりきず) = a scrape or graze.
cards.example_sentence: 弟は自転車で転んで、ひじを擦りむいた。
cards.example_reading: おとうと は じてんしゃ で ころんで、 ひじ を すりむいた。
cards.example_meaning: My little brother fell off his bike and scraped his elbow.

cards.scene: Fits the throbbing pain of 三葉's scrapes and bruises after the fall.
cards.context: A pulsing pain that beats with your heart: 頭がずきずきする, 傷がずきずき痛む. Compare ひりひり (stinging, like a burn), ちくちく (prickly), がんがん (a pounding headache).
cards.example_sentence: 転んだところが、夜になってもずきずき痛む。
cards.example_reading: ころんだ ところ が、 よる に なって も ずきずき いたむ。
cards.example_meaning: The place where I fell is still throbbing, even at night.

cards.scene: Lying at the bottom of the slope, 三葉 is overcome with despair.
cards.context: 絶 (cut off) + 望 (hope). 絶望する, 絶望的 (hopeless), 絶望の淵 (the depths of despair). Opposite: 希望 (hope). A heavy word that narration saves for the lowest point.
cards.example_sentence: 何度挑戦してもうまくいかず、彼は絶望しかけた。
cards.example_reading: なんど ちょうせん して も うまく いかず、 かれ は ぜつぼう しかけた。
cards.example_meaning: No matter how many times he tried it didn't work, and he nearly gave in to despair.

cards.scene: After the fall, 三葉 seems to have nothing left and lies there unable to go on.
cards.context: 力 (strength) + 尽きる (run out). Written style for giving out completely: ゴール直前で力尽きる. In literary prose it can also mean to die, so read the context.
cards.example_sentence: マラソンの選手は、ゴールの手前で力尽きて倒れた。
cards.example_reading: マラソン の せんしゅ は、 ゴール の てまえ で ちからつきて たおれた。
cards.example_meaning: The marathon runner collapsed, spent, just short of the finish line.

cards.scene: Fits tears welling up and blurring 三葉's sight as she lies there in despair.
cards.context: Liquid spreading and blurring: インクが滲む, 涙で景色が滲む, 血が滲む (blood oozes). Figurative: 声に悔しさが滲む (frustration seeps into one's voice). The kanji 滲 is rare — know the kana form.
cards.example_sentence: 涙で、手紙の文字が滲んで見えた。
cards.example_reading: なみだ で、 てがみ の もじ が にじんで みえた。
cards.example_meaning: Through my tears, the writing in the letter looked blurred.

cards.scene: Fits tears spilling down 三葉's face in her lowest moment.
cards.context: Big tears dropping one after another: 涙がぽろぽろこぼれる. Also crumbs or small bits falling off: パンくずがぽろぽろ落ちる. Quiet weeping is しくしく; loud wailing is わんわん.
cards.example_sentence: 映画の最後で、四葉はぽろぽろと涙をこぼした。
cards.example_reading: えいが の さいご で、 よつは は ぽろぽろ と なみだ を こぼした。
cards.example_meaning: At the end of the movie, Yotsuha's tears spilled down one after another.

cards.scene: 三葉 opens her hand, expecting to find his name written on her palm — and finds something else.
cards.context: One-kanji spelling of 手のひら (both read てのひら); literary prose prefers 掌. Other readings: たなごころ (archaic) and しょう in compounds (合掌 = palms pressed together in prayer). 掌を返す = to do a sudden about-face.
cards.example_sentence: 雪のひとひらが、掌の上ですっと溶けた。
cards.example_reading: ゆき の ひとひら が、 てのひら の うえ で すっと とけた。
cards.example_meaning: A single snowflake melted away on my palm.

cards.scene: Fits 三葉 closing her hand tight over the words on her palm.
cards.context: 握る (grip) + 締める (tighten); also written 握り締める. 拳を握りしめる (clench a fist), 手紙を握りしめる. Often with ぎゅっと: ぎゅっと握りしめる.
cards.example_sentence: 彼女はお守りをぎゅっと握りしめて、試験会場に入った。
cards.example_reading: かのじょ は おまもり を ぎゅっと にぎりしめて、 しけん かいじょう に はいった。
cards.example_meaning: She clutched her lucky charm tightly and walked into the exam hall.

meanings: to clench one's teeth and endure
cards.scene: Fits 三葉 forcing herself back onto her feet after reading her palm.
cards.context: 食いしばる = to clench (the teeth) hard. Enduring pain or hardship, physically or figuratively: 歯を食いしばって耐える / 頑張る. A classic gesture of resolve in action scenes.
cards.example_sentence: 苦しいときこそ、歯を食いしばって前に進もう。
cards.example_reading: くるしい とき こそ、 は を くいしばって まえ に すすもう。
cards.example_meaning: It's exactly when things are hard that we should grit our teeth and push on.

cards.scene: Fits 三葉's exhausted legs shaking as she pushes herself up and runs on.
cards.context: Violent, uncontrollable shaking of joints: 膝ががくがくする, 足ががくがく震える (from fear, cold or fatigue). Also for something loose: 歯ががくがくする (a wobbly tooth).
cards.example_sentence: 初めての舞台で、緊張のあまり足ががくがく震えた。
cards.example_reading: はじめて の ぶたい で、 きんちょう の あまり あし が がくがく ふるえた。
cards.example_meaning: On stage for the first time, my legs shook from sheer nerves.

cards.scene: Fits 三葉 staggering to her feet and on toward the town office.
cards.context: From よろよろ (unsteady). Losing your balance for a moment: 疲れてよろめく, 段差でよろめく. ふらつく is similar; よろける is a close colloquial variant.
cards.example_sentence: 電車が急に止まり、立っていた人たちがよろめいた。
cards.example_reading: でんしゃ が きゅう に とまり、 たって いた ひと たち が よろめいた。
cards.example_meaning: The train stopped suddenly and the standing passengers staggered.

cards.scene: Fits 三葉 facing her father squarely at the town office.
cards.context: 見る + 据える (set firmly). To look steadily without wavering: 相手の目を見据える. Figurative: 将来を見据える (keep the future firmly in view) — a favourite in speeches and news.
cards.example_sentence: 選手は静かにゴールを見据えて、スタートの合図を待った。
cards.example_reading: せんしゅ は しずか に ゴール を みすえて、 スタート の あいず を まった。
cards.example_meaning: The athlete quietly fixed her eyes on the finish line and waited for the starting signal.

cards.scene: 三葉 reaches the town office ready to face her father, whatever happens.
cards.context: 覚悟する / 覚悟を決める (to make up one's mind, steel oneself). Implies accepting a hard outcome in advance — stronger than 決心 (decision). 覚悟しろ! is a classic threat: 'Prepare yourself!'
cards.example_sentence: 厳しい練習になることは、覚悟の上だ。
cards.example_reading: きびしい れんしゅう に なる こと は、 かくご の うえ だ。
cards.example_meaning: I'm fully prepared for the training to be tough.

cards.scene: Fits the instant the fragment falls — a blinding flash.
cards.context: 閃 (flash) + 光 (light). An intense, instantaneous burst: 閃光が走る. Used for explosions, lightning and camera flashes. 閃く (ひらめく) = to flash; also, for an idea to strike you.
cards.example_sentence: 空に閃光が走り、数秒遅れて雷の音が響いた。
cards.example_reading: そら に せんこう が はしり、 すうびょう おくれて かみなり の おと が ひびいた。
cards.example_meaning: A flash streaked across the sky, and a few seconds later the thunder boomed.

cards.scene: Fits the deafening roar as the fragment comes down.
cards.context: 轟 (three 車 — rumbling carts) + 音. 轟音を立てる, 轟音とともに. The verb 轟く (とどろく) = to roar, resound; also to be famous far and wide (名が轟く).
cards.example_sentence: 飛行機が轟音を立てて、頭の上を通りすぎた。
cards.example_reading: ひこうき が ごうおん を たてて、 あたま の うえ を とおりすぎた。
cards.example_meaning: The plane passed overhead with a thunderous roar.

cards.scene: Aftermath (may fall at the start of Ch.8): people call it a miracle that most of the town survived.
cards.context: 奇 (strange) + 跡 (trace). 奇跡的に (miraculously), 奇跡が起きる. Don't confuse it with the homophone 軌跡 (きせき, trajectory). In the story, only the reader knows the 'miracle' had a cause.
cards.example_sentence: 大事故だったが、乗客は奇跡的に全員助かった。
cards.example_reading: だいじこ だった が、 じょうきゃく は きせきてき に ぜんいん たすかった。
cards.example_meaning: It was a major accident, but miraculously every passenger survived.

cards.scene: Aftermath (may fall at the start of Ch.8): reports note that most of the townspeople survived.
cards.context: 生 (live) + 存 (exist). Formal and news register: 生存者 (survivor), 生存率 (survival rate), 生存が確認される. Everyday equivalents: 生き残る, 助かる.
cards.example_sentence: 地震から三日後、がれきの中から生存者が見つかった。
cards.example_reading: じしん から みっか ご、 がれき の なか から せいぞんしゃ が みつかった。
cards.example_meaning: Three days after the earthquake, a survivor was found in the rubble.

cards.scene: Aftermath (may fall at the start of Ch.8): most of the townspeople come through safely.
cards.context: 無 (without) + 事 (incident). 無事に着く (arrive safely), 無事を祈る (pray for someone's safety), ご無事で (stay safe). Everyday too: 無事終わった (it went off without a hitch).
cards.example_sentence: 台風が過ぎて、家族全員の無事が確認できた。
cards.example_reading: たいふう が すぎて、 かぞく ぜんいん の ぶじ が かくにん できた。
cards.example_meaning: After the typhoon passed, we confirmed that the whole family was safe.

cards.scene: The safe place the townspeople must reach for the plan to work — and where survivors gather afterwards.
cards.context: 避難 (evacuation) + 所 (place). Japanese towns designate schools and community halls as shelters. On signs, 避難場所 is an open-air assembly point, while 避難所 is a building where people can stay.
cards.example_sentence: 地震のあと、近くの小学校が避難所になった。
cards.example_reading: じしん の あと、 ちかく の しょうがっこう が ひなんじょ に なった。
cards.example_meaning: After the earthquake, the nearby elementary school became an evacuation shelter.

cards.scene: Aftermath (may fall at the start of Ch.8): the townspeople survived because an evacuation drill happened to be held that night.
cards.context: 訓 (instruct) + 練 (practise). 避難訓練 (evacuation drill) and 防災訓練 (disaster drill) are routine in Japanese schools and towns. 訓練 suggests organised, repeated practice; 練習 is general practice.
cards.example_sentence: 学校では年に二回、避難訓練が行われる。
cards.example_reading: がっこう で は ねん に にかい、 ひなん くんれん が おこなわれる。
cards.example_meaning: Evacuation drills are held at school twice a year.

cards.scene: Aftermath (may fall at the start of Ch.8): the striking fact that most of Itomori's people survived.
cards.context: 大 (big) + 半 (half): 'more than half'. 〜の大半 = most of ~: 町民の大半, 一日の大半. A little more formal than ほとんど, and used for amounts clearly over half rather than 'almost all'.
cards.example_sentence: 休みの日の大半を、ゲームをして過ごしてしまった。
cards.example_reading: やすみ の ひ の たいはん を、 ゲーム を して すごして しまった。
cards.example_meaning: I ended up spending most of my day off playing games.
